rows.description: A five-year-old is refused a second sweet and feels the world unfair. Her body reacts before her words, with shouting "I hate you" and stamping.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3

rows.description: She tries crying, promising and finally shouting, watching whether the limit will move. If it moves after a tantrum, she learns that tantrums work, and the pattern grows stronger.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3

rows.description: The parent, tired after work, feels stung by "I hate you" and is tempted to punish or match the child's volume. Noticing his own heat and taking a breath first is the key moment.
graph_context: next stage: Calm and firm limit
this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3
related mind states: tiredness, relief from stress

rows.description: He says "I hear you are angry. The answer is still no more sweets today." He does not shame her, bargain or shout, and stays available for comfort.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3
related mind states: anger, shame, calm

rows.description: After crying she climbs into his lap, ashamed and relieved. The child needs to know that anger did not break the bond, and any harsh words did not make her unlovable.
graph_context: previous stage: Calm and firm limit
next stage: Reflection and skill building
this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3
related mind states: sadness, anger, shame, relief

rows.description: Later they talk through what to do when angry, such as stomping softly, drawing or asking for a hug. The parent may also apologise for raised voice, modelling repair and teaching that everyone can make things right.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3

rows.description: A teacher notices a quiet student's careful questions in science and offers extra reading. Being noticed by an adult who is neither parent nor friend can feel surprising, and quietly powerful, to the teen.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26

rows.description: The student turns up at the teacher's desk after school with doubts about becoming a doctor. She tests whether the teacher will take her seriously or laugh, and each respectful reply lowers her guard.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: amusement, admiration, doubt

rows.description: She copies his phrases and treats his opinions as the truth. Admiration is a real motor of growth, though it can hide the mentor's limits and the student's own judgement.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26

rows.description: The teacher critiques her project bluntly, and she feels stung and briefly angry. A good mentor holds high standards with warmth, and the student learns that criticism from someone who cares is a gift.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
